key_insight: Curvature-Scaled SAM controls gradient distortion under generalized smoothness, enabling convergence guarantees beyond standard smoothness assumptions.
engineering_relevance: Scaling both perturbations and descent steps by curvature upper bounds offers a principled way to stabilize sharpness-aware training.
method: Quantify how SAM perturbations distort the original gradient.
Use curvature upper bounds to scale perturbations and descent steps.
Prove deterministic O(1/T) stationarity and convex-gap rates, plus linear convergence under the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition.
evidence_signal: In minibatch computer vision experiments, the (H0,H1) variant achieved the highest mean best-test accuracy in all four settings against tuned SAM and USAM using constant and cosine-annealing schedules.
watch_item: The convergence guarantees are deterministic; practical minibatch performance also depends on selecting suitable curvature upper bounds.
paper_title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness
